llm.summary: The real-estate skill kit is mostly coherent, but its helper tools allow unscoped local template file reads and writes, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: tools/ruleengine.py accepts absolute or existing paths for user templates and writes template names without path normalization, allowing user-supplied values to read JSON files or write .json files outside the intended my_templates directory. render.py also derives output paths from config-controlled identifiers without normalization.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: install.sh is user-invoked and copies a rendered skill into detected agent skill directories, then records a SHA-256 hash. I found no hidden network fetch, destructive command, or automatic execution, but it does modify agent skill state.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Generated templates include broad configurable trigger keywords and commercial conversion flows. They also include privacy and compliance guardrails, but installers should narrow triggers and review any generated brand skill before enabling it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is limited to explicit generated output, saved user templates, and user-run installation into an agent skills directory. The persistence is disclosed, but the template path handling is broader than the stated template-storage purpose.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe a Chinese real-estate advisor skill generator with templates, mock adapters, and calculators. Sales, CRM, lead conversion, and financial estimate behaviors are disclosed as part of the real-estate business purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable reviewing the generated skill and running local helper scripts. Narrow trigger keywords, verify all mortgage/tax policy numbers against official local sources, avoid rendering untrusted brand.yaml files, and do not pass untrusted template names or paths to the calculator tools until template path validation is fixed.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted for tools/ruleengine.py:185-190. Loading a named user template is expected, but accepting absolute or arbitrary existing paths is not proportionate to the my_templates feature. I found no automatic exfiltration or hidden execution.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted for tools/ruleengine.py:177-182. Saving templates is expected, but raw template names can traverse out of the intended directory and write .json files elsewhere. This supports Review, not maliciousness.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded for brand.example.yaml. Configurable trigger keywords are part of the generator design, but generic housing terms should be narrowed by users before publishing a generated skill.
[SQP-1] expected: Partially accepted for examples/developer/yunlu.sales.yaml. The sales example has broad terms such as price and unit-type concepts; this is disclosed example configuration, but it could over-activate a promotional workflow if installed unchanged.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded for examples/kunming/kunming.buy.yaml. The example is city/domain specific and editable, though some real-estate terms remain broad enough to warrant review before use.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded for template/archetypes/consumer-buy.md.tmpl. The trigger template is explicit and configurable; risk depends on the generated brand.yaml values rather than hidden behavior in the template.
[SQP-1] expected: Partially accepted for template/archetypes/developer-sales.md.tmpl. Sales-oriented generated skills need precise project-specific triggers because the template is meant to convert users to visits and leads.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted for template/modules/content-marketing.md.tmpl. Turning repeated customer questions into marketing topics fits the module purpose, but the template should more explicitly require aggregation and removal of identifying details.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Accepted as a documentation gap for tools/README.md. The quick claim of nationwide applicability and precision is too strong for demo real-estate policy calculators, although later caveats and runtime warnings reduce the risk.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Partially accepted for tools/README.md. Quick-start commands appear before the strongest demo-grade warning, but the tools themselves print an estimate/compliance warning and the rules file labels values as demo data.
